standard.when: Only work that repeats what NexKit already does, in the same way: a change to docs, skills or tests only, or a fix inside one module that follows a pattern the module already has. It changes no decision of the engine, no prompt, no protocol schema, no config key or command, and nothing about tokens, secrets, markers, redaction or who may run a command. Anything else is hard.

hard.when: Everything that is not standard. That covers a change to the engine's states or decisions, the protocol's schemas, the GitHub host's calls of the engine, the import of NexKit 6's markers, prompts and their goldens, runtimes and pins, publishing, merging, retries and autopilot, and anything a mistake in which could let an agent write with a token, leak a secret, pass a marker that NexKit did not write, or start, repeat or merge work no rule allows. When unsure between standard and hard, choose hard.

checklist: The change keeps every rule of docs/writing-docs.md: read the page and check the diff, code included, against each of its rules, and its Docs: line names every doc section the change makes false, each fixed

A setting, command, label, status or prompt contract that the change adds, renames or removes changes with its tests, docs and skills in the same change, and a search of docs/, skills/ and AGENTS.md finds no old name
Every behaviour the change adds or changes has a test that fails without it; a new automatic rule has a scenario in tests/test_scenarios.py, and a new engine rule a case in tests/conformance/

A job that runs an agent or repository code keeps a read-only token and no App key, and text from an agent, a comment or CI is validated, passed through redact.py and never read as a marker, as AGENTS.md's Rules say

A decision about what happens next to a work item that the engine holds is made only in nexkit/engine/, and a change that moves one keeps NexKit 6's behaviour as docs/testing.md's Moving decisions into the engine says

checklist.text: The change adds no exception to a check and loosens none
